pets:ashgut:combatAbility.name: Gorge
pets:ashgut:description: A swollen, soot-lined thing that breathes in the smoke you cook through. It steadies the flame so nothing chars — and when your health dips, it pushes a little more nourishment into every mouthful.
pets:ashgut:name: Ashgut
pets:carapace:combatAbility.name: Bulwark
pets:carapace:description: An ancient, shell-plated thing that has outlasted every blade aimed at it. Standing near it, some of that patience settles into your own hide, blunting every blow before it lands — and every so often it plants itself fully between you and the strike, and nothing gets through at all.
pets:carapace:name: Carapace
pets:carrionwing:combatAbility.name: Death Dive
pets:carrionwing:description: It circles every fight before landing. Feathers the colour of old rot, talons built for hanging on. Its scavenger's eye picks over a kill twice before it's satisfied, some nights doubling what you carry home — then it folds its wings and drops, a dive that punches clean through armour.
pets:carrionwing:name: Carrionwing
pets:charnel:combatAbility.name: Feast of the Fallen
pets:charnel:description: Born of a mass grave that forgot how to stay still. Every kill you land feeds it a mouthful — and it presses a little vitality back into your chest for the trouble. Mid-fight it feasts properly: a burst that tears at the enemy and fills you back up in the same bite.
pets:charnel:name: Charnel
pets:cragmaw:combatAbility.name: Boulder Toss
pets:cragmaw:description: A blind, stone-jawed burrower that cracks ore in pairs — veins split at the seam. Its layered hide drinks blows in combat with the indifference of mountain granite.
pets:cragmaw:name: Cragmaw
pets:flayling:combatAbility.name: Flay
pets:flayling:description: It wears its own hide inside out and does not seem to mind. At the tanning rack it coaxes more leather from every hide — and in combat it finds the gap in every armour and peels it back.
pets:flayling:name: Flayling
pets:gemwraith:combatAbility.name: Prismatic Lance
pets:gemwraith:description: A hollow shape that has filled itself with stolen facets. It bleeds light from a dozen cuts — and at the cutting table it sometimes coaxes a second gem from the very same stone. In battle that precision becomes something crueller.
pets:gemwraith:name: Gemwraith
pets:gillrot:combatAbility.name: Hook & Tear
pets:gillrot:description: A pallid thing that drags itself between worlds. It surfaces twice the catch from black water — and in a fight it hooks deep and tears something loose.
pets:gillrot:name: Gillrot
pets:gloomrat:combatAbility.name: Pilfer
pets:gloomrat:description: Grease-slick and shadow-shaped, it fits through gaps that should not exist. It turns your hands to ghost-touch — and robs its combat quarry of loose coin mid-bite.
pets:gloomrat:name: Gloomrat
pets:glyphmaw:combatAbility.name: Rune Feast
pets:glyphmaw:description: It swallows runes whole and regurgitates more than it consumed. The throat-glow never fades. In combat it feeds on each blow like a leech with a hunger for mana rather than blood.
pets:glyphmaw:name: Glyphmaw
pets:gorehound:combatAbility.name: Maul
pets:gorehound:description: A battle-bred thing that lives at the edge of the kill. A tithe of every wound you open flows back to you, thin but real — and its own strikes score deep enough to bleed long after the blow lands.
pets:gorehound:name: Gorehound
pets:hemlock:combatAbility.name: Venom Phial
pets:hemlock:description: A root-bound familiar pickled in its own secretions. It lingers at your side and breathes a faint numbing mist — sparing potions and making every toxin you deal seep deeper and linger longer.
pets:hemlock:name: Hemlock
pets:hoarspite:combatAbility.name: Grave Frost
pets:hoarspite:description: Pure spite condensed into winter. It holds a grudge against warmth and vents it slowly into your mana reserves — then exhales that grudge onto your enemies as a rime that stiffens joints and slows the kill.
pets:hoarspite:name: Hoarspite
pets:ironmaw:combatAbility.name: Body Slam
pets:ironmaw:description: Jaws like a bear-trap, neck like a siege-block. Standing at your side, it lends its raw brawn straight into your arms — and in a fight it rams the ground so hard the enemy's next blow comes late.
pets:ironmaw:name: Ironmaw
pets:pyreling:combatAbility.name: Flame Nova
pets:pyreling:description: Something was burned alive and refused to scatter. It orbits you in a slow heat-smear and bleeds warmth into your mana without being asked — then reaches through every strike you land to leave a coal behind.
pets:pyreling:name: Pyreling
pets:quillshrike:combatAbility.name: Quill Volley
pets:quillshrike:description: A hollow-boned predator that impales its kills on its own quills. At the crafting bench it coaxes extra materials from every batch — and its eye for weak points makes your ranged crits land truer.

pets:rotbark:combatAbility.name: Root Snare

quests:chronicle_01:description: Gather 25 items of any kind at Emberhold's gate: your first steps under the Warden's watch.
quests:chronicle_01:loreText: The Chronicle has gone a long time without a new name. Today it carries yours — or what you leave in its place: the Nameless, taken in at the gate of Emberhold, in the rain, carrying nothing. I have shown you the forge, the garden beds, the vault, the notice board. Ambrast, they say, lives in every hearth, and Maera in every seed; whether they listen is not mine to record. What is recorded: you set your hands to work. Small labors, none of them great, every one of them a beginning. The first page is the easiest. It only has to begin.
quests:chronicle_01:name: The First Page
quests:chronicle_02:description: Hunt 15 pasture animals and bring down the Maddened Bull: the gentlest land ahead of you already answers back.
quests:chronicle_02:loreText: The livestock of the Pastures has taken up customs of its own, since no one is left to object. The bull was no spawn of the ash — only a beast that went too long unanswered. You answered. The Chronicle passes no judgement on the herds; they stayed when the people left, out of loyalty or lack of imagination, and it records neither. It records this: first blood, yours and not yours, and that your hand grew steadier instead of faster. That is rare. The Pastures are the kindest country you will see from here on. I do not write that as a warning. I write it because it is true.
quests:chronicle_02:name: First Blood
quests:chronicle_03:description: Drive out the Imp nesting in the greenest corner of the Pastures.
quests:chronicle_03:loreText: In the greenest corner of the Reach nests a spark from elsewhere. The old folk used to say: where an imp dwells, a stranger has passed by. The old folk are gone; the imp was still there. You have driven it out. It will return, sparks always do, but the Chronicle needs the pattern, not the victory: even the green land has cracks, and the cracks have an origin. I wrote the word "stranger" and held the pen for the space of a breath. It does not usually do that. Record it as a quirk of the chronicler. Or as the first honest word in this book.
quests:chronicle_03:name: The Spark in the Grain
quests:chronicle_04:description: Walk the abandoned march and thin the goblin warband: 30 rank and file, 8 of their fel-touched casters.
quests:chronicle_04:loreText: The march had ramparts, armories, watchfires: the shield-wall of the Reach. Through its needle's eye came the fleeing: orc clans with anvils on their backs, Rakhari caravans with seed, and at last no one at all. Then the march was abandoned, and nowhere is it written who gave the order. The goblins did not come as conquerors; they came as heirs, and out of the estate they are building a mockery of the old army. Their fel magicians carry a fire that came from no forge of the Reach — borrowed, says the warband, and will not name the creditor. You walked the old border, as I asked. Who abandoned it, the Chronicle carries as an open entry. It has practice.
quests:chronicle_04:name: The Empty March
quests:chronicle_05:description: End the Warchief's campaign in the Goblin Warband dungeon before it earns a name.
quests:chronicle_05:loreText: The Warchief dreams of making the warband an army again. It would be funny if he were not so diligent. You walked his muster in its own order: vanguard, spearwall, siege line, blood rite, and took from him the seal the band grants its officers. An army whose seal can be taken is not an army. The march was abandoned once; a second time will not be recorded. I enter the campaign that will now never earn a name, and note, for the sake of order: the fel fire did not die with the Warchief's ambitions. It has only changed debtors.
quests:chronicle_05:name: The War Banner
quests:chronicle_06:description: Cull the vermin of the Ashfields and lay 10 mire wisps to rest: the unburied field hands of a dead harvest.
quests:chronicle_06:loreText: I led you here on purpose. This is what a land looks like when an idol has loved it: miles of grey, the stubble of old harvests, and what lives here lives on leavings. The scriptures called these fields the Grain Mother's bread-land; no one ever prayed here in vain — so it was believed. The wisps in the mire are the field hands nobody buried, once burying went out of fashion. They are still praying, I fear. And here is the lesson I marched you through ash to learn: none of it ever reached the Grain Mother. Not one stalk, not one prayer. The harvest flowed elsewhere. Mark the direction. The Chronicle has, for a long time now.
quests:chronicle_06:name: The Ash Lesson
quests:chronicle_07:description: Break the Ash Tyrant's law of the grey: the greatest carrion-beast of the Ashfields.
quests:chronicle_07:loreText: Over the fields ruled the Ash Tyrant, the greatest carrion-beast of the grey, a king by the only law the ash acknowledges: what feeds, reigns. You broke that law. The Chronicle has grown careful with kings; the Reach had some, and their chapters all end alike. But it gladly records that an order holds in the grey again, one that does not feed on it. It is little. In the Ashfields, little is a great deal. The vultures will crown a new tyrant; that is their way. He will be smaller, for a while. Whiles are what we defend. I write down every one.
quests:chronicle_07:name: The Carrion King
quests:chronicle_08:description: Thin the rootlings of the Blackthorn Wood and contest the Elder Treant: passage, not victory, is what the wood is owed.
quests:chronicle_08:loreText: The wood alone learned something from the Idolfall: it armed itself. Rootlings pull free of the underbrush, gnarled and thorned, and the Elder Treant is less a tree than a verdict. I asked for passage, not victory — the difference will matter, the deeper this book leads. You contested the verdict and thinned the briar, no more. The Blackthorn will remember; woods keep their own chronicle, in rings instead of lines. Beneath its roots lie barrows older than any keep of the Reach, and out of them comes a singing. We follow it. I wish I could write: reluctantly.
quests:chronicle_08:name: Thorns
quests:chronicle_09:description: Silence 15 Barrow Chanters and pass the Forest Warden: the dead's song points cryptward.
quests:chronicle_09:loreText: For the first time you have heard the dead sing. The Barrow Chanter chants litanies in a tongue no one speaks anymore, and does not tire; the Bramble Witch was a woman who stayed when everyone left, and the wood is content with the trade. The Forest Warden bears an office that people once held — the wood repossessed it and filled the post anew. You respected the office, and you passed; the Chronicle records both. And it records what I do not like: the singing has a direction. Cryptward. The dead singing can be borne. The dead singing toward something is a question. We are going to ask it.
quests:chronicle_09:name: The Choir Beneath the Barrows
quests:chronicle_10:description: Survey the Crypt's broken order: 40 skeleton guards, 10 of the Hollow Choir that sings no amen.
quests:chronicle_10:loreText: The Order of the Grave Wardens gathered the dead of the Reach into a single deep and sealed them, orderly, indexed, watched, as Vhel would have it. The seal held generations longer than the Order did. I know those corridors; I walked them while the Order still dug. Do not reckon how long ago that must have been — the Chronicle doesn't either. Now the deep stands open, and the dead are "fit for duty" again: warriors, archers, ice-mages, a garrison that asks no pay. The Hollow Choir goes on singing the prayers of the dead; hollow, because no amen ever comes. You have surveyed the order of things and understood the breach. That will do for today. It will not do for tomorrow.
quests:chronicle_10:name: The Broken Seal
quests:chronicle_11:description: Strike down the Necromancer Lord in the Depths of the Crypt: a victory that does not feel like one.
quests:chronicle_11:loreText: He who broke the seal was no intruder. By every sign, he was the Order's last castellan, grown tired of waiting. Or whispered tired: the voice that talked him out of his vigil may not have been his own. You struck off the hand that broke the seal. I write it as a victory because it is one, and I write beside it that it does not feel like one — not to you, not to me. You cannot put down a warden who was left alone too long without inheriting the question: who left him alone, and who spoke to him when no one else still did? The file stays open. It is used to that.
quests:chronicle_11:name: The Lord of the Depths
quests:chronicle_12:description: Hold your own against 30 giants of the Wildwood: wolves and stags grown past any human measure.
quests:chronicle_12:loreText: The Wildwood is the last fat land of the Reach. Every living thing the ash drove out crowded here, and then the wood did what woods do: the strong ate the weak, generation upon generation, until only giants were left. Nothing here is cursed, nothing corrupted — that is the unsettling part. The Wildwood is healthy. It is simply no longer built for people. You held your own where man is no longer the crown of creation: grey wolves the size of ponies, stags like monuments. The Chronicle needs that proof, and I will tell you why. What waits at the end of this book does not count man as the crown either. It counts him as the field.
quests:chronicle_12:name: The Giants
quests:chronicle_13:description: Complete the old royal hunt: 3 Dire Wolves loose in the Wildwood, then the Old One of the Wildwood waiting in the Wildwood Hunt dungeon.
quests:chronicle_13:loreText: The Reach once had kings. The hunt is what remains of their dignity, and it deserved to be hunted properly to its end — Kaenor's right, say the scriptures, and the wood keeps count. It began with the howling; then the Great Stag stood, then the Dire Wolf, and at the last the Old One of the Wildwood himself. No revenge, no campaign: a rite. You proved nothing to the wood, the Wildwood is not vain, but you proved it to the Chronicle. The fang lies beside me as I write: one entry of dignity in an undignified age. I have weighed it twice. It weighs what it should.
quests:chronicle_13:name: The Old Hunt
quests:chronicle_14:description: Lay 20 Reef Drowned and 10 Tide Sirens to rest: the chapter called 'Flight' closes for good.
quests:chronicle_14:loreText: When the world fell, fleets put out to sea: humans, orcs, Rakhari, whoever found a deck. Somewhere, so people prayed, there must be land no idol ever loved. The sea has been giving them back ever since, corpse by corpse, plank by plank. The drowned walk the shoals like a wage that was never paid out; the siren sings their names — the only registry the sea keeps. The devout say she sings it to Nereth. No one knows whether he listens. I closed the chapter called "Flight" today, for good, and entered the names, as many as the siren would yield. Someone has to. The Chronicle takes in the dead as well. It is not particular. It is faithful.
quests:chronicle_14:name: What the Sea Gives Back
quests:chronicle_15:description: Face both faces of the Slag Pit: 10 Iron Revenants in the ember stalls, 10 Frost Hexers in the cold veins below.
quests:chronicle_15:loreText: Here they smelted whatever veins the land would yield, up to that ore from which the wreaths of the graven images were cast. I must add to the Chronicle something I have carried alone for a lifetime: I stood in these smelteries, back then, at the casting of the first wreaths. And I saw a man who was not one. He guided the founders' hands, and his shadow did not flicker with the fire. I gave warning. No one listens to a priest of silent gods. So I began to write things down. This book is not a chronicle, Nameless. It is a witness's testimony — kept against a defendant with no name. Now you know it too.
quests:chronicle_15:name: The Cold Forge
quests:chronicle_16:description: Climb the Highlands: 25 rocs, 8 Gravecliff Specters where the veil runs thin. The rocs evade every clumsy blade. Without precision, nothing lands a hit up here.
quests:chronicle_16:loreText: The ash is heavy and stays below; that is why the sky up here is still clean, Skorai's hall, the scriptures said, and everything that could fly has fled upward. But height has a price: up here the veil is thin — worn thin by one who crossed it too often. The Gravecliff Specter haunts the cliffs where the Highlands gave their dead to the wind; you can almost see through the Void Roc, and what you see is not flesh. You will have noticed that I grow short of words. The Chronicle notes that I do not need to look up the way. I have been following it all my life.
quests:chronicle_16:name: The Thin Sky
quests:chronicle_17:description: Break the Stormbringer's watch over the Highland Aerie and clear the skyway.
quests:chronicle_17:loreText: The great aerie of the rocs is tiered like a fortress: the Aerie Warden, the Hunting Wing, the Elder, and in the eye of the weather the Stormbringer, whose core holds more sky than any bird is owed. Up here I understood: a nest is built around the brood. This one is built around the pass, every eye on the road to the Idol Hall. These birds are not nesting. They stand watch — and no watch posts itself. In the file I keep a line open for whoever posted it. I pity the birds sincerely; they are the healthiest thing the Reach still has, and they stand in the way of what is necessary. The keeper of the Chronicle may afford pity, but not the detour. The skyway is clear, the storm's core in your hand. We climb on.
quests:chronicle_17:name: The Aerie
quests:chronicle_18:description: Clear the Wyvern Lair and bring down the Void Roc: the last gate before the Hall stands open.
quests:chronicle_18:loreText: In the high nesting grounds, where the veil is thinnest, the wyverns brood, and above them waits the Void Roc, half bird, half hole in the world. The void gathers what belongs to the idols the way magpies gather silver, though nobody asked it to. You brought it down, and the high grounds went quiet behind you. Beyond the lair lies only the Hall. I have not written that sentence in a very long time. The pen managed it all the same. Onward, then — the file wants its ending, and I promised it one.
quests:chronicle_18:name: The Last Gate
quests:chronicle_19:description: End the Last Idol's trial in the Sanctum, and find the maker's marks behind the throne. Do not enter without runes on your armor: unprotected, none withstand the Sanctum.
quests:chronicle_19:loreText: The full passage, wave upon wave: the Idol's warden, the veil, the scaled wall, and the throne. The Last Idol held no conversation; it held proceedings, and its three blades were its three tenors: Judgement, Vengeance, Condemnation. You have ended the trial the world has conducted against itself since the Idolfall. Behind the throne we found what no iconoclasm ever found: maker's marks in the god-iron, set by a hand that was not human. The Last Idol was never the world's judge. It was another's work — and the other is still here. I write with a steady hand, except for one word. Culprit: known.
quests:chronicle_19:name: The Judgement
quests:chronicle_20:description: Face the true culprit behind the throne: the final battle of the first volume.
quests:chronicle_20:loreText: He stepped out of the shadow of his broken masterwork, and the Chronicle received what it never had: a face and a name. Drazhan the Crownless, son of a god and a mortal woman, cheated of both; the idols his siege-works against heaven, mankind never his enemy, only his field. That is what makes him unforgivable. You beat him back, step by step, until the Hall had nothing left to give him. He did not fall. He chose retreat the way a field commander does, and left us his words: "Mark this day. You have seen a retreat, not a fall. When the gods come at last — tell them I started it." I have written the line this book waited generations for. The first volume closes. The next page is already laid in.
quests:chronicle_20:name: The True Culprit
quests:chronicle_21:description: Climb to floor 5 of the Paragon Spire: the tower Drazhan left behind.
quests:chronicle_21:loreText: The tower did not stand there before Drazhan withdrew. Afterward it stood there: his work left behind, greater than all the treasures, a drill-yard in which the ash rehearses everything the Reach has ever suffered, floor upon floor, harder and higher. A rehearsal for armies that do not yet march. The reprieve your victory bought must be defended, and the defense is led by whoever climbs. I do not climb. I wait below, the second volume open on my knees, and I enter floors as if they were chapters. No topmost storey is known. One thing still belongs in the first volume: of the seven broken crowns on Drazhan's chain, one bore no name the scriptures still keep. The sky that kept silent so long will have to answer. The God Wars are coming — and the Chronicle does not end. It only gets a second volume.
quests:chronicle_21:name: Epilogue: The Second Volume

quests:q_crypt_3:description: Skeleton Ice Mages haunt the Crypt's deepest vaults. Destroy 10 of them before they freeze you solid.
quests:q_crypt_3:name: Frozen Silence
quests:q_dire_wolf_hunt:description: Dire Wolves stalk the deep Wildwood, larger than any wolf should be. Slay 15 of these ferocious predators.
quests:q_dire_wolf_hunt:name: Terror of the Wilds
quests:q_fighter_1:description: Defeat 75 enemies in total. Blood and sweat forge the fighter Emberhold needs.
quests:q_fighter_1:name: Seasoned Fighter
quests:q_fighter_2:description: Cut down 200 enemies in total. The Servants have started to remember your name.
quests:q_fighter_2:name: Hardened Warrior
quests:q_fighter_3:description: Defeat 500 enemies in total. Every foe you fell is an entry the ash never gets to keep.
quests:q_fighter_3:name: Veteran of a Hundred Battles
quests:q_first_blood:description: Slay 10 goblins in the Borderlands; they've been raiding the last farms near Emberhold long enough.
quests:q_first_blood:name: Goblin Blood
quests:q_first_steps:description: Cull 5 chickens on the Pastures outside Emberhold, a first grip on a weapon, nothing more.
quests:q_first_steps:name: First Steps
quests:q_frost_hound:description: Frost Hounds prowl the Frost Caverns, where the pit dug too deep and struck the cold of the void. Hunt 15 of them.
quests:q_frost_hound:name: The Cold Hunt
quests:q_gatherer_2:description: Gather 5,000 items in total for Emberhold. This land gives what little it has left only to those who endure.
quests:q_gatherer_2:name: Relentless Collector
quests:q_gatherer:description: Gather 50 items of any kind for Emberhold: chop wood, mine ore, pick herbs, or fell monsters.
quests:q_gatherer:name: Gatherer
quests:q_goblin_slayer:description: Push the goblin warband further back: slay 30 goblins in the Borderlands, once the shield-wall of the Reach.
quests:q_goblin_slayer:name: Goblin Slayer
quests:q_miner_1:description: Reach Mining level 5 and open richer veins for Emberhold's forge.
quests:q_miner_1:name: Pick and Stone
quests:q_miner_2:description: Reach Mining level 30. The deeper veins of the Borderlands demand a stronger arm.
quests:q_miner_2:name: Iron Will
quests:q_miner_3:description: Reach Mining level 50. The rarest ores of the Reach lie deep beneath the surface, deeper than ever before.
quests:q_miner_3:name: Deep Earth Calling
quests:q_moss_golem_hunt:description: Moss Golems have taken the forest clearings; even the wood keeps guards now. Shatter 15 of them.
quests:q_moss_golem_hunt:name: Mossy Menace
quests:q_roc_fledgling:description: Roc Fledglings rule the Highland thermals, where the sky still runs clean. Take down 10 of these colossal birds.
quests:q_roc_fledgling:name: Highland Skywatch
quests:q_shaman_hunt:description: The goblin shamans tap Dim Essence from the old watchfires and stir the warband to war. Silence 10 of them.
quests:q_shaman_hunt:name: Shaman Hunt
quests:q_skiller_1:description: Reach a combined total level of 20 across all skills; Emberhold counts every capable hand twice.
quests:q_skiller_1:name: Jack of All Trades
quests:q_skiller_2:description: Reach a combined total level of 50. Knowing only one trade doesn't last long in this world.
quests:q_skiller_2:name: Versatile Adventurer
quests:q_skiller_3:description: Reach a combined total level of 75. Many roads led you here, and Emberhold forgets none of them.
quests:q_skiller_3:name: Seasoned Adventurer
quests:q_skiller_4:description: Reach a combined total level of 100. Few who set out from Emberhold have come this far.
quests:q_skiller_4:name: Path of Mastery
quests:q_skiller_5:description: Reach a combined total level of 150. Your deeds are told by Emberhold's fire now, the way the legend of the Hearthforge once was, where every craft of the Reach wintered out the world's fall.
quests:q_skiller_5:name: Legend of the Hearthforge
quests:q_slagpit_1:description: Venture into the Slag Pit, where god-iron was once smelted, and exterminate 20 Pit Spiders lurking in the shadows.
quests:q_slagpit_1:name: Into the Pit
quests:q_slagpit_2:description: Iron Revenants patrol the deepest passages, smiths who died in their armor and were never told to stop. Strike down 10 of these undying constructs.
quests:q_slagpit_2:name: Iron Haunting
quests:q_smith_journeyman:description: Reach Smithing level 20. Emberhold's forge rewards patience: master the basics before tackling harder metals.
quests:q_smith_journeyman:name: Journeyman Smith
quests:q_smith_master:description: Reach Smithing level 50. Only the truly dedicated can work the rarest metals of the Reach: god-iron forgives no impatience.
quests:q_smith_master:name: Master of the Forge
quests:q_stag_hunter:description: Wild stags like monuments dominate the Wildwood Hunting Grounds. Bring down 20 of these proud beasts.
quests:q_stag_hunter:name: King of the Wood
quests:q_thorn_wolf_pack:description: The Thorn Wolves of the Blackthorn Wood are more dangerous than their kin; the wood has sharpened them. Slay 20 of them.
quests:q_thorn_wolf_pack:name: Thorn Wolf Pack
quests:q_wolf_slayer:description: Hunt 15 gray wolves in the Wildwood Hunting Grounds; everything here has grown larger since no one hunts anymore.
quests:q_wolf_slayer:name: Into the Wildwood
quests:q_woodcutter_1:description: Reach Woodcutting level 5. A sharp axe and a stout heart are all it takes; Emberhold asks no more.
quests:q_woodcutter_1:name: Into the Wood
quests:q_woodcutter_2:description: Reach Woodcutting level 15 to fell oaks; the camp needs more than thin kindling.
quests:q_woodcutter_2:name: Seasoned Lumberjack
quests:q_woodcutter_3:description: Reach Woodcutting level 30. The ancient groves yield their secrets only to the worthy; the Blackthorn prefers reverence to haste.
quests:q_woodcutter_3:name: Master of the Axe
